title: Regular-section exact sequences give lower-dimensional differences
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty proper locally Noetherian scheme over a field $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with finite dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with no embedded associated points and support equal to $X$. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $K_X$ for the total-quotient sheaf obtained by localizing $\mathcal O_X$ at its non-zero-divisors, and $K_X(\mathcal L):=K_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L$ for its meromorphic-section sheaf. Let $s$ be a meromorphic section of $\mathcal L$ such that the canonical map $K_X\to K_X(\mathcal L)$ given by $1\mapsto s$ is injective (this is the regular-meromorphic-section condition), and let $\mathcal I$ be its denominator ideal, the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$ whose sections $a$ satisfy $a s\in\mathcal L$. Then the canonical maps $\mathcal I\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal I\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L$ are injective and their cokernels $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal Q'$ are coherent with $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal Q)),\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal Q'))<\dim X$. Moreover, for every integer $n$, $\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes(n+1)})-\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=\chi(X,\mathcal Q'\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})-\chi(X,\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$.

proof.text: The assertion is local on X. By clause (1) of [lem-sc-hilbert-denominator-ideal-nowhere-dense], X is covered by affine opens U = Spec(A) on which L is trivial, s is a/b with a and b non-zero-divisors of A, and I(U) = {x in A | x(a/b) in A}. The module of sections M of F is finite, has support all of Spec(A), and has no embedded associated primes. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-affine-denominator-module] to obtain injective maps I M \to M and I M \to M (the latter representing multiplication by s), with cokernels annihilated by I and by s(I). These local maps agree on overlaps, so they glue to the two canonical maps in the statement. [lem-sc-hilbert-denominator-ideal-nowhere-dense] supplies the quasi-coherent denominator ideal and says that V(I) and the support of O_X/s(I) are contained in closed nowhere-dense subsets.

On an affine Noetherian open U, the affine auxiliary identifies I(U) with an ideal of the Noetherian ring O_X(U), so it is finitely generated; hence the quasi-coherent ideal I is of finite type and coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. The product I F is quasi-coherent and has affine sections I(U) F(U) by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections]. As a quasi-coherent submodule of the coherent module F, I F is coherent by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. The same lemma then makes the cokernels of the maps I F to F and F tensor L coherent; F tensor L is coherent because L is locally free of rank one and tensoring is locally finite free on affine trivializations.

proof.text: The first cokernel is annihilated by I, so its support is contained in V(I), and the second is annihilated by s(I), so its support is contained in the closed support supplied by [lem-sc-hilbert-denominator-ideal-nowhere-dense]. Both closed sets are nowhere dense. Since X is nonempty, locally Noetherian, and finite-dimensional, [lem-sc-hilbert-nowhere-dense-dimension-drop] gives dimension strictly less than dim X for both supports.

proof.text: For every integer n, tensor the short exact sequence 0 \to I F \to F \to Q \to 0 by L^n, and tensor the short exact sequence 0 \to I F \to F tensor L \to Q' \to 0 by L^n. Tensoring by the invertible module L^n is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the two resulting short exact sequences: the common middle term I F tensor L^n cancels, yielding chi(X, F tensor L^(n+1)) - chi(X, F tensor L^n) = chi(X, Q' tensor L^n) - chi(X, Q tensor L^n).
